untertitel_admin: Detect external USB and SATA drives, mount them with one click, eject safely or format – NTFS, exFAT, ext4 and more.
untertitel_nutzer: Connected drives and their status. Only the admin can mount and eject.
lade_fehl: The drives could not be read.
keine: No external drive connected. Plug in a USB disk or stick – it appears here automatically.
keine_hinweis: Supported: NTFS, exFAT, FAT32, ext2/3/4, btrfs and XFS; HFS+ read-only.
freigabe_ohne_rechte_hinweis: The network share is disabled because nobody has rights yet. Under “Shares”, enter who may read or write – then the drive becomes visible on the network (Mac, Windows, Linux).
system_hinweis: Part of the system disk – managed by FAH-NAS and cannot be changed here.
ohne_fs_hinweis: This drive has no known file system. Format it first.
einhaengen_erklaerung: The drive is mounted at /data/shares/<Name> and is then visible in the file manager.
name: Name
name_erklaerung: Lowercase, 1–32 characters from a–z, 0–9, - and _. Becomes the folder name under /data/shares and – if desired – the share name.
name_fehler: Name: lowercase, 1–32 characters from a-z, 0-9, - and _
nur_lesen_erklaerung: The drive is mounted write-protected. Useful for backups that must not be changed.
nur_lesen_hfsplus: FAH-NAS can only read HFS+ (Mac) – writing is not possible on this file system.
automatisch_erklaerung: Remembers the drive and mounts it again automatically the next time it is plugged in or after a restart.
freigabe_erklaerung: Creates a network share with the same name so Mac, Windows and Linux see the drive directly. You can read and write right away; add other people under “Shares”.
hinweis_ohne_rechte: {fs} has no Linux permissions: all users with access can read and write everything. Per-file rights are not available here.
hinweis_mit_rechten: {fs} supports per-file rights. After mounting, the drive's root belongs to the group fahnas-nutzer.
auswerfen_erklaerung: Open files are written, then the drive is unmounted. Afterwards you can unplug it.
auswerfen_vergessen_erklaerung: Removes auto-mount and the share for this drive and powers it off. Otherwise it stays known and is mounted again the next time it is plugged in.
ausgeworfen: “{name}” has been ejected. You can unplug it now.
belegt_titel: The drive is still in use
belegt_erklaerung: These programs have files open on it. Close them (or the network connection) and try again.
vergessen_frage: Forget “{name}”? Auto-mount and share will be removed; the data on the drive stays untouched.
einstellungen_erklaerung: Read-only takes effect at the next mount. Auto-mount and share take effect immediately.
formatieren_warnung: Warning: formatting irreversibly erases ALL data on {pfad}. There is no recycle bin and no snapshot.
formatieren_fs_erklaerung: Determines which devices can read the drive later.
fs_exfat_erklaerung: exFAT: readable and writable by Mac, Windows and Linux, including files over 4 GB. No per-file rights. The best choice for removable drives.
fs_ext4_erklaerung: ext4: Linux standard with per-file rights, robust and fast. Mac and Windows cannot read it without extra software.
fs_btrfs_erklaerung: btrfs: like the NAS data disk – checksums and snapshots possible. Only for drives that stay on the NAS.
fs_ntfs_erklaerung: NTFS: Windows standard, read-only on Mac. Choose it if the drive is mainly used with Windows computers.
formatieren_label_erklaerung: Required. The name the drive shows on other devices. Starts with a letter or digit, followed by letters, digits, spaces, - and _; exFAT up to 11, ext4 up to 16, btrfs and NTFS up to 32 characters.
formatieren_label_fehler: Label: required, starts with a letter or digit, followed by letters, digits, spaces, - and _ – at most {max} characters for {fs}.
formatieren_tippen: Type the device name to confirm
formatieren_tippen_erklaerung: Protection against accidents: the button is enabled only once “{name}” is entered here.
smart_fehl: The S.M.A.R.T. values could not be read. USB enclosures often don't pass them through.
raid_erklaerung: Combine several internal disks into one pool – with redundancy. A pool appears as its own share.
raid_zu_wenig_platten: A pool needs at least two additional internal disks (SATA/NVMe). USB disks are not suitable and are not offered.
raid_name_erklaerung: Also becomes the share name, e.g. data.
raid_erkl_raid0: All disks combined, full capacity – if one fails, everything is lost. Only for data you have elsewhere.
raid_erkl_raid1: Every disk holds everything. Capacity of one disk; all but one may fail. From 2 disks.
raid_erkl_raid5: One disk of parity spread over all. Good middle ground from 3 disks; one may fail.
raid_erkl_raid6: Two disks of parity – two may fail at the same time. From 4 disks, recommended for large disks.
raid_erkl_raid10: Mirrored pairs, fast and safe. From 4 disks (even number); one per pair may fail.
raid_mindestens: This level needs at least {n} disks.
raid_mindestens_gerade: This level needs at least {n} disks, an even number.
raid_warnung_loeschen: All data on the selected disks will be erased!
raid_angelegt: Storage pool created – the initial sync runs in the background; the pool can be used right away.
raid_ersetzen_erklaerung: The new disk takes the place of the failed one; then the pool rebuilds.
raid_ersatz_erklaerung: The spare disk steps in automatically when a disk fails.
raid_warnung_neue: All data on the new disk will be erased.
raid_pruefung_gestartet: Data check started – it runs in the background.
raid_loeschen_warnung: All data in pool “{name}” will be lost; the disks will be wiped.
neu_frage: New disk detected – what would you like to do with it?
neu_erklaerung: Mounting keeps the data. A storage pool erases the disk. As a backup destination it is mounted and the “Set up a backup” assistant opens.
raid_erweitern_erklaerung: New disks are added, then the pool reshapes in the background. It stays usable; the extra space is available once the reshape is done.
raid_erweitern_art_erklaerung: RAID 5 gives more space, another mirror more redundancy.
raid_erweitern_gestartet: Reshape running – this can take hours. You will be notified when it is done.
raid_vergroessern_frage: Use the extra space of the larger disks in “{name}”? The pool then syncs the new area.
raid_vergroessern_laeuft: The pool is growing – you will be notified when it is done.
import_titel: Take over storage from another NAS
import_erklaerung: For switching from UGOS, Synology & co.: the disks stay as they are. FAH-NAS mounts the RAID and volumes and turns the chosen folders into shares – no formatting, no deleting.
import_suchen_laeuft: Searching disks and looking at them read-only
import_export_tipp: Switching from UGOS: first run “python3 ugos-export.py” on UGOS (in the FAH-NAS release under tools/). The wizard then suggests the previous permissions per folder.
import_trennen_text: Detach “{name}”? The shares {liste} disappear from FAH-NAS and the volume is unmounted.
import_trennen_sicher: Nothing is deleted on the disks – the data stays as it is and can be taken over again at any time.
import_getrennt: Volume detached – the data is unchanged on the disks
import_sicher: Safe: nothing is formatted, partitioned or deleted. Only owners and permissions of the taken-over folders change – the contents stay unchanged. Tip: back up the most important data first.
import_nichts_gefunden: No foreign storage found. Are the disks plugged in? FAH-NAS assembles RAIDs and volume groups itself while searching.
import_raid_warnung: This RAID is degraded (a disk is missing). Taking over still works – replace the disk soon.
import_export_gefunden: UGOS export found (created {zeit}) – permissions per folder are suggested from it. Please check.
import_export_fehlt: No UGOS export on this volume – the previous permissions cannot be read without UGOS. Set them below yourself (default: admins only).
import_rechte_erklaerung: Who may see or change this folder after taking over. Admins may always do everything.
import_schnappschuesse_titel: btrfs subvolume: FAH-NAS can take snapshots of it.
import_freigabename_erklaerung: The folder's name on the network afterwards (lower case, a–z, 0–9, - and _).
import_intern: Not taken over (belongs to the old system): {liste}
import_besitzer_erklaerung: The old accounts have different numbers on FAH-NAS. Choose who owns the files of each old account afterwards – access itself follows the permissions above. Anything unassigned belongs to root.
import_konten_fehlen: These users do not exist on FAH-NAS yet: {liste}. Create them under Users with the same name and search again – otherwise they get no access.
import_bestaetigung: Understood: contents stay unchanged, owners and permissions of the chosen folders are set anew.
import_laeuft: Taking over folders and transferring permissions
import_name_ungueltig: Share name for “{ordner}” is invalid (lower case, a–z, 0–9, - and _, at most 32).
import_name_belegt: Share name for “{ordner}” is already taken or reserved.
import_fertig_tipp: The shares are listed under Shares. You can now delete the file fahnas-ugos-export.json in a folder.
import_or_uebernehmen: Take over rights of {anzahl} {anzahl|subfolder|subfolders} (as folder rights)
import_rechte_lassen_app: Recommended: this folder holds data of Docker apps. Databases and the like check who owns their files – transferring the rights would stop the apps from starting. Sharing and network access still work.
import_rechte_lassen_erklaerung: Meant for app data only: files keep their previous owners and rights. Folder rights from UGOS are then not taken over.
import_app_daten_titel: Compose files of Docker apps live here.
import_heime_erklaerung: Each personal folder of the old NAS becomes the personal folder of the chosen FAH-NAS user – only that user sees it (on the network as \\NAS\<name>). Files stay on the volume, nothing is copied. If the user already has a personal folder with content on FAH-NAS, nothing is laid over it.
import_alter_pfad_erklaerung: Compose files and scripts from the old NAS address folders as /volume1/…. With the old path they find them unchanged – required for the Docker takeover. It is only mounted additionally, nothing is moved.
import_alter_pfad_belegt: Something already exists at {pfad} on FAH-NAS – the old path is not laid over it. Choose another one or leave it out.
import_name_heim_doppelt: A user gets two personal folders (“{ordner}”) – please choose only one per user.
import_name_alter_pfad: Old path “{ordner}” invalid – allowed are /volume1 to /volume99.
import_raid_pruefen_titel: Reads all disks and compares them – runs in the background, the NAS stays usable. The system also checks once a month on its own.
import_raid_pruefen_gestartet: Check started – you will get a notification with the result.
import_raid_ersetzen_text: A disk of “{name}” is missing or faulty. The new disk gets the same layout as a healthy one and is added; the RAID then rebuilds in the background.
import_raid_spiegel_titel: Turns a RAID 1 with one disk (UGOS “Basic”) into a mirror with two disks – afterwards it survives the failure of one disk.
import_raid_spiegel_text: “{name}” gets an additional disk as mirror. All data is then stored twice; if a disk fails, nothing is lost.
import_raid_neue_platte_erklaerung: Only free disks (not system, no RAID, not mounted). It must be at least as large as the others.
import_raid_keine_platte: No free disk found. Insert the new disk and open the dialog again.
import_raid_alte_platte_erklaerung: Is removed from the RAID. FAH-NAS never swaps a working disk – the RAID would be without redundancy during the rebuild.
import_raid_loescht: Everything on the new disk is deleted. FAH-NAS does not touch disks with traces of another RAID or LVM.
import_raid_bestaetigen: For safety: type the name of the new disk
import_raid_bestaetigen_erklaerung: For example “sdc” – so you do not pick the wrong disk by accident.
import_raid_ersetzen_laeuft: Disk is being prepared and added
import_raid_ersetzen_fertig: Disk added – the rebuild runs in the background. You will get a notification when it is done.
ort_titel: Storage locations for Docker, apps and VMs
ort_erklaerung: Docker, app folders and VMs normally live on the system disk. Here you move them to a taken-over volume (e.g. a large SSD) – paths stay the same, apps do not notice.
ort_docker_erklaerung: All images, containers and Docker volumes. Grows with every app – a small system disk fills up quickly.
ort_apps_erklaerung: Settings and data of catalogue apps and ZIP apps.
ort_vms_erklaerung: Disk images and ISOs of the VMs.
ort_ziel_erklaerung: Taken-over volume or back to the system disk. Enough space must be free – FAH-NAS checks this first.
ort_docker_haelt: Docker is off during the move – all apps stop and start again by themselves afterwards. Depending on size this takes minutes to hours.
ort_vms_aus: All VMs must be shut down for this.
ort_sicher: Safe: data is copied, not moved. The previous location stays; if anything fails, everything keeps running as before. You delete the old copy on the system disk yourself afterwards.
ort_fertig: Moved – everything runs at the new location.
ort_kein_ziel: No taken-over volume mounted – first take over storage above.
ort_keine_volumes: Moving works onto taken-over volumes (card above).
ort_nicht_aktiv: The volume of this location is currently not mounted – Docker or the VMs will not start until it is back (so nothing lands on the system disk).
ort_alt_loeschen_titel: Frees space on the system disk – afterwards there is no way back to it.
ort_alt_loeschen_text: Delete the old copy of “{bereich}” on the system disk? It has not been used since the move; without it there is no quick way back.
ort_alt_geloescht: Old copy deleted – the space on the system disk is free.
